fields.description:
## Problem

`fixture_selection.select_from_corpus` eagerly compiles full ticket state for EVERY
review-bearing ticket before selection, via `reader(ticket_id, tracker)` (default
`labels._read_ticket_state_via_env_override`, which calls `show_ticket(ticket_id,
include_inbound=True)`). At full corpus scale this is ~6s/ticket x ~1957 unique tickets
≈ **~3 hours of pure CPU** before a single candidate is emitted — and the live admission
runner (`fixture_admission`) pays this same cost upfront on every run.

Measured this session (impl-693 worktree, full committed corpus): a single
`_read_ticket_state_via_env_override` call is ~5–7s; the selection loop compiled state for
1957 unique tickets; a stubbed reader completes the identical candidate selection in ~57s.

## Why it's expensive and why it's avoidable

`ticket_state` is consumed in selection ONLY by `_escaped(review)` →
`labels.escaped_defect(state)`, which needs just two things: `close_class == "plan_defect"`
and any inbound `caused_by` link. The full `show_ticket(include_inbound=True)` reducer is far
more than that. The candidate SET and tier split are provably independent of ticket_state
(tier derives from fire/no_fire signals: reproduction/author_response/margin); `escaped_defect`
only affects the rank tiebreak (2nd sort key in `_candidate_sort_key`).

The corpus event loader (`corpus._load_ticket_events`) does NOT carry STATUS/LINK events, so a
cheap batched `escaped_defect` index cannot be built from it directly — the fix needs either a
batched store read of close_class + caused_by edges, or lazy per-ticket compilation restricted
to only the tickets actually referenced by emitted candidates.

## Approach

Compile `escaped_defect` (or the minimal ticket_state it needs) lazily/batched instead of
eagerly for all review-bearing tickets:
- Option A (lazy): defer state compilation until a review is about to become an emitted
  candidate, so only the small candidate-referenced ticket set pays the cost.
- Option B (batched): one store-wide pass building `{ticket: close_class}` and a reverse
  `caused_by` index, then an O(1) `escaped_defect` lookup per ticket.

Preserve behaviour: candidate set, tiers, ranks (incl. escaped-defect promotion) must be
byte-identical to the current eager path over the same committed history.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `select_from_corpus` over the full committed corpus completes in minutes, not hours,
      with NO per-review-bearing-ticket `show_ticket(include_inbound=True)` fan-out — verified
      by a test asserting the reader/compile is invoked only for candidate-referenced tickets
      (or replaced by a batched index), not for all review-bearing tickets.
- [x] Emitted manifest rows (candidate set, tier, direction, rank, escaped_defect) are
      byte-identical to the current implementation over a fixed fixture corpus — verified by a
      regression test comparing old vs new output.
- [x] `escaped_defect` fidelity is preserved: a ticket closed `plan_defect`, and a ticket named
      by an inbound `caused_by`, both still rank-promote — verified by a held-out test.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
      pass.

## Provenance

Discovered during REB-693 (epic 65dd / spin-cub-usher) ticket 67aa AC10: the live admission
run's selection step took >54 min CPU and was on track for ~3h before the norm-less findings
even reached the solver. The AC10 live run was completed with a stubbed `read_ticket_state`
(escaped_defect=False) as a documented fidelity compromise (candidate set + tiers identical;
rank tiebreak only); this ticket is the real-fidelity + performance fix.

## Completion evidence (2026-09-03) — Gerrit change 2590 MERGED

- **AC1 (minutes not hours, no per-ticket fan-out)** — MET, and satisfied more strongly than written. `test_default_path_never_compiles_per_ticket_state` monkeypatches the reader to RAISE and the default path never touches it AT ALL, which is stronger than "only for candidate-referenced tickets". Measured on the real corpus: **74.2s wall** (build_corpus 24.8s, findings load 23.2s, index build 6.6s, select_candidates 14.3s) versus ~2h15m eager — about **110x**.
- **AC2 (byte-identical)** — MET, and the comparison runs the REAL old path: `test_manifest_is_byte_identical_to_the_eager_per_ticket_path` runs `select_from_corpus` twice over a 4-ticket git-backed fixture, the old side passing `read_ticket_state=labels._read_ticket_state_via_env_override` — the actual callable that used to be the default, not a stub and not a snapshot generated from the new code — then writes both manifests and compares bytes. Mutation-checked: breaking the reverse `caused_by` index made it fail along with three others.
- **AC3 (escaped_defect fidelity)** — MET. Held-out test: both escaped candidates (one closed `plan_defect`, one named by an inbound `caused_by`) outrank a clean candidate that owns the lower uuid tiebreak, with tier and margin equal — so only the escaped-defect sort key can explain the order. Plus an index-versus-real-reader agreement test, ticket by ticket.
- **AC4 (gates)** — MET. `make lint` exit 0 (mechanism ratchet new=0), `make typecheck` clean over 750 files, `check_complexity_baseline.py --check` new=0 increased=0. Targeted suite 243 passed / 3 skipped.

## Two corrections to this ticket's own analysis

1. **Option A (lazy) was NOT viable**, though this ticket named it as one of two approaches. `escaped_defect` is a union over all backing reviews — `_fire_rows` unions over `_unique_reviews(reviews_for_norm)`, and `_no_fire_rows` unions over `silent`, which is every review store-wide that routed the criterion without firing. Measured union: **1554 of 1960 review-bearing tickets = 79%**. Lazy would have saved ~20%, not three hours. The plan-review gate flagged this scope ambiguity before implementation, which is what prompted measuring it rather than assuming.
2. **The stated constraint about `corpus._load_ticket_events` not carrying STATUS/LINK is true but NOT binding.** The working-tree reducer gives both facts directly in 6.6s store-wide, so no git-object walk was needed.

## The actual quadratic, which this ticket did not name

`reducer/_inbound.py::_mentioning_dirs` byte-scans every event file of every ticket per subject, and `show_ticket(include_inbound=True)` calls it once per ticket. `labels.build_escaped_ticket_index` inverts the loop: one pass building both facts instead of n passes each scanning n.

One deliberate behaviour difference, documented in the docstring: where the eager reader RAISED (absent ticket, error/fsck_needed status, no CREATE), the index reports not-escaped rather than aborting the whole selection. This cannot change any row the old path successfully produced, because in that case it produced no rows at all. Verified the skip surface directly — `reduce_ticket` raising still propagates loudly; only a non-dict return is defensively skipped, and absence means NOT escaped, the conservative direction.

Side benefit: the batched path avoids `show_ticket` entirely, so it no longer touches the store's freshness/reconverge path — the eager measurement emitted `CrossSessionWarning` on tickets held by other agent sessions, which this stops provoking.
